metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets Romania

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 results for Romania using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of schools and students, and OECD typically provides sampling weights and replicate weights for variance estimation; however, this factsheet does not specify the exact weight variables or replicate method. The reported uncertainty statements (e.g., 95% confidence intervals) indicate that standard PISA variance estimation procedures were applied in the production of the database tables. For analysts reproducing these estimates, the recommended approach is to use the OECD-provided weights/replicate weights from the PISA 2022 Database and to apply the same plausible-value and scaling procedures used for PISA achievement reporting.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive OECD factsheet summarising PISA 2022 creative thinking results rather than an empirical modelling study that specifies plausible-value (PV) and missing-data handling procedures. The factsheet reports scaled scores, proficiency levels, and associations (e.g., correlations and explained variance) that are already computed in the OECD PISA 2022 Database tables, without detailing the PV combination or missing-data strategy used to generate those table outputs. As a result, the PV and missing-data handling are not reported at the level of methodological transparency required for replication.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample for Romania consists of 7,364 students in 262 schools who completed the PISA 2022 assessment in mathematics, reading, or science, representing about 162,000 15-year-olds (an estimated 76% of the total population of 15-year-olds). The factsheet does not describe additional exclusions beyond the standard PISA implementation and the database table construction.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III (Creative Minds, Creative Schools) factsheet summarises Romania’s performance on the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking cognitive test for 15-year-olds. The creative thinking test comprises 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating/improving ideas) across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). Romania’s mean creative thinking score is 26 on a 60-point scale, significantly below the OECD average of 33. The factsheet reports proficiency distribution (58% at Level 3 or above; 14% at Level 5 or 6) and relative strengths/weaknesses across ideation processes and domain contexts, including higher relative performance in generating creative ideas and in written/visual expression. It also documents within-Romania gaps by socio-economic status (15.1 score-point advantage for top quartile vs bottom quartile) and a gender gap favouring girls (2.1 points), alongside associations between creative thinking and mathematics/reading performance. Because this is a descriptive factsheet, it does not provide an ML modelling pipeline or replication details for PV/missing-data handling beyond the OECD database table outputs.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is for an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet (a descriptive reporting product) rather than an empirical paper that trains or evaluates machine learning models. Consequently, there is no study-specific ML algorithm list, no explicit PV combination or missing-data procedure described in the text, and no model-based target-variable prediction results to tabulate as StructuredFinding rows. The factsheet instead reports pre-computed PISA database estimates (scores, proficiency levels, correlations, and explained variance) and provides methodological cautions for the special PISA 2022 implementation context (COVID-19-related delays and sampling-standard caveats for some countries/economies).
